claim_records.text: ViT achieves inferior performance to CNNs when trained from scratch on a midsize dataset like ImageNet.
The simple tokenization of input images in ViT fails to model important local structure such as edges and lines among neighboring pixels, leading to low training sample efficiency.
The redundant attention backbone design of ViT leads to limited feature richness for fixed computation budgets and limited training samples.

T2T-ViT incorporates a layer-wise Tokens-to-Token (T2T) transformation that progressively structurizes the image to tokens by recursively aggregating neighboring Tokens into one Token, such that local structure represented by surrounding tokens can be modeled and tokens length can be reduced.
T2T-ViT reduces the parameter count and MACs of vanilla ViT by half, while achieving more than 3.0% improvement when trained from scratch on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT outperforms ResNets and achieves comparable performance with MobileNets by directly training on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT with comparable size to ResNet50 (21.5M parameters) achieves 83.3% top1 accuracy at image resolution 384×384 on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT-14, T2T-ViT-19 and T2T-ViT-24 are designed to have comparable parameters with ResNet50, ResNet101 and ResNet152 respectively.

T2T-ViT-7 and T2T-ViT-12 are lite models with comparable model size to MobileNetV1 and MobileNetV2, with no special efficient convolution designs and only reduced layer depth, hidden dimension, and MLP ratio.

Five architecture designs borrowed from CNNs were explored for ViT backbone: Dense connection as DenseNet, deep-narrow vs. shallow-wide structure as in Wide-ResNets, channel attention as Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks, more split heads in multi-head attention layer as ResNeXt, and Ghost operations as GhostNet.

claim_records.text: Among the explored CNN-inspired designs, the deep-narrow structure is the most efficient and effective for ViT, reducing parameter count and MACs significantly with nearly no degradation in performance.

claim_records.text: HIRI-ViT upgrades prevalent four-stage ViT to five-stage ViT tailored for high-resolution inputs.
HIRI-ViT decomposes typical CNN operations into two parallel CNN branches in a cost-efficient manner.
HIRI-ViT achieves 84.3% Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with 448×448 inputs under comparable computational cost of approximately 5.0 GFLOPs.
HIRI-ViT with 448×448 inputs improves iFormer-S with 224×224 inputs by 0.9% Top-1 accuracy.
HIRI-ViT is built upon the seminal idea of decomposing the typical CNN operations into two parallel CNN branches in a cost-efficient manner.
HIRI-ViT achieves to-date the best published Top-1 accuracy of 84.3% on ImageNet with 448×448 inputs under comparable computational cost of approximately 5.0 GFLOPs.
HIRI-ViT absolutely improves 83.4% of iFormer-S by 0.9% with 224×224 inputs.
HRViT and HRFormer target for constructing Vision Transformer with multi-scale inputs by keeping all resolutions throughout the network and performing cross-resolution interaction.
The inputs of HRViT and HRFormer ViT backbones are still limited to a small resolution of 224×224.
IRDS-a first uses a strided 3 × 3 convolution to expand the dimension and reduce the spatial size, and then a 1×1 convolution is utilized to shrink the channel dimension.
IRDS-b is similar to inverted residual block, with the difference that only normalization and activation operations are applied after the first convolution.
HIRI-ViT constructs three variants in different model sizes: HIRI-ViT-S (small size), HIRI-ViT-B (base size), and HIRI-ViT-L (large size).
The entire architecture of HIRI-ViT is composed of one HR-stem layer and five stages.
For the first two stages with high-resolution inputs, HIRI-ViT replaces conventional Transformer blocks with light-weight High Resolution blocks to avoid huge computational overhead.
For the third stage, HIRI-ViT leverages only CFFN blocks to handle the middle-resolution feature maps.
HIRI-ViT employs Transformer blocks in the last two stages with low-resolution inputs.
Simply enlarging the input resolution of prevalent ViT backbones will introduce practical challenge especially the sharply increased computational costs.

HIRI-ViT absolutely improves 83.4% of iFormer-S by 0.9% with 224×224 inputs.
HRViT and HRFormer target for constructing Vision Transformer with multi-scale inputs by keeping all resolutions throughout the network and performing cross-resolution interaction.
The inputs of HRViT and HRFormer ViT backbones are still limited to a small resolution of 224×224.
IRDS-a first uses a strided 3 × 3 convolution to expand the dimension and reduce the spatial size, and then a 1×1 convolution is utilized to shrink the channel dimension.
IRDS-b is similar to inverted residual block, with the difference that only normalization and activation operations are applied after the first convolution.
HIRI-ViT constructs three variants in different model sizes: HIRI-ViT-S (small size), HIRI-ViT-B (base size), and HIRI-ViT-L (large size).
The entire architecture of HIRI-ViT is composed of one HR-stem layer and five stages.
For the first two stages with high-resolution inputs, HIRI-ViT replaces conventional Transformer blocks with light-weight High Resolution blocks to avoid huge computational overhead.
For the third stage, HIRI-ViT leverages only CFFN blocks to handle the middle-resolution feature maps.
HIRI-ViT employs Transformer blocks in the last two stages with low-resolution inputs.
Simply enlarging the input resolution of prevalent ViT backbones will introduce practical challenge especially the sharply increased computational costs.

claim_records.text: CrossViT proposes a dual-branch transformer to combine image patches of different sizes to produce stronger image features.

CrossViT processes small-patch and large-patch tokens with two separate branches of different computational complexity and these tokens are then fused purely by attention multiple times to complement each other.
CrossViT's cross-attention token fusion module uses a single token for each branch as a query to exchange information with other branches.
CrossViT's proposed cross-attention only requires linear time for both computational and memory complexity instead of quadratic time otherwise.
On the ImageNet1K dataset, CrossViT outperforms DeiT by a large margin of 2% with a small to moderate increase in FLOPs and model parameters.
CrossViT's cross-attention module uses a single token for each branch as a query to exchange information with other branches.
CrossViT's proposed cross-attention only requires linear time for both computational and memory complexity instead of quadratic time otherwise.
On the ImageNet1K dataset, CrossViT outperforms DeiT by a large margin of 2% with a small to moderate increase in FLOPs and model parameters.
Vision Transformer (ViT) requires very large datasets such as ImageNet21K and JFT300M for training.
DeiT shows that data augmentation and model regularization can enable training of high-performance ViT models with fewer data.
CrossViT proposes a dual-branch transformer to combine image patches of different sizes to produce stronger visual features for image classification.
CrossViT processes small and large patch tokens with two separate branches of different computational complexities and these tokens are fused together multiple times to complement each other.
CrossViT's cross-attention module allows for linear-time generation of the attention map in fusion instead of quadratic time otherwise.
CrossViT outperforms DeiT by a large margin of 2% with a small to moderate increase in FLOPs and model parameters.
CrossViT performs better than or on par with several concurrent works based on ViT, and demonstrates comparable results with EfficientNet with regards to accuracy, throughput and model parameters.

BoTNet replaced the spatial convolutions with global self-attention in the final three bottleneck blocks of a ResNet resulting in models that achieve a strong performance for image classification on ImageNet benchmark.
Vision Transformer (ViT) is the first convolution-free transformer-based method to match or even surpass CNNs for image classification.
T2T-ViT introduces a layer-wise Tokens-to-Token (T2T) transformation to encode the important local structure for each token instead of the naive tokenization used in ViT.
Multi-scale features have shown to benefit CNNs, but their applicability for vision transformer still remains as a novel and largely under-addressed problem.
CrossViT proposes a dual-path architecture to extract multi-scale features for better visual representation with vision transformers.

claim_records.text: PVT+RetinaNet achieves 40.4 AP on the COCO dataset, surpassing ResNet50+RetinaNet (36.3 AP) by 4.1 absolute AP with a comparable number of parameters.
PVT-Large achieves 42.6 AP, which is 1.6 points better than ResNeXt101-64x4d, with 30% less parameters.
The dense prediction task aims to perform pixel-level classification or regression on a feature map, with object detection and semantic segmentation as two representative dense prediction tasks.
PVT's four-stage output feature maps have strides of 4, 8, 16, and 32 pixels with respect to the input image, forming a feature pyramid {F1, F2, F3, F4}.

PVT uses a progressive shrinking strategy via patch embedding layers to control the scale of feature maps, unlike CNN backbones that use different convolutional strides to obtain multi-scale feature maps.

The entire PVT model is divided into four stages, each comprised of a patch embedding layer and a Li-layer Transformer encoder, with output resolution progressively shrinking from 4-stride to 32-stride.

PVT is a unified backbone for various vision tasks without convolutions, usable as a direct replacement for CNN backbones, and boosts performance on downstream tasks including object detection, instance and semantic segmentation.

claim_records.text: ViT-CoMer-L achieves 64.3% AP on COCO val2017 without extra training data, and 62.1% mIoU on ADE20K val, both comparable to state-of-the-art methods.
ViT-CoMer-L achieves 62.1% mIoU on ADE20K val, comparable to state-of-the-art methods.
ViT-CoMer is a plain, pre-training-free, feature-enhanced ViT backbone with Convolutional Multi-scale feature interaction that facilitates bidirectional interaction between CNN and transformer.
ViT-CoMer-T with 29M parameters achieves 47.1 APb on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, compared to ViT-Adapter-T (28M, 46.0 APb) and MixFormer-B3 (35M, 46.2 APb).
ViT-CoMer-S with 50M parameters achieves 48.8 APb on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, and reaches 52.1 APb when using advanced pre-trained weights (denoted by †).
ViT-CoMer-B with 129M parameters achieves 50.2 APb on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, and reaches 54.2 APb when using advanced pre-trained weights (denoted by †).
ViT-CoMer-L† with 363M parameters achieves 55.9 APb on COCO val2017 using Mask R-CNN, outperforming ViT-Adapter-L† (348M, 52.1 APb) and ViT-L† (338M, 48.3 APb).
ViT-CoMer-L with advanced pre-training achieves 64.3% AP on COCO val2017 without training on extra detection data such as Objects365, which is the best record on this setting.
ViT-CoMer attains 62.1% mIoU on ADE20K val with advanced pre-training, comparable with state-of-the-art methods.
In ViT-CoMer's weight initialization process, the ViT module directly uses open-source pre-training, and the rest of the modules use random initialization.

ViT-CoMer designs two core modules: the Multi-Receptive Field Feature Pyramid module (MRFP) to supplement ViT with more abundant multi-scale spatial information, and the CNN-Transformer Bidirectional Fusion Interaction module (CTI) to fuse multi-scale features from CNN and Transformer.

claim_records.text: BoB benchmarks a diverse suite of pretrained models including vision-language models, self-supervised learning trained models, and the Stable Diffusion backbone across computer vision tasks ranging from classification to object detection to OOD generalization.
BoB's comprehensive analysis was conducted on more than 1500 training runs.

Among the models considered in BoB, convolutional neural networks pretrained in a supervised fashion on large training sets still perform best on most tasks, despite the increasing popularity of vision transformers and self-supervised learning.
In apples-to-apples comparisons on the same architectures and similarly sized pretraining datasets, SSL backbones are highly competitive.

Across the full BoB evaluation suite spanning tasks, datasets, and settings including ID and OOD, supervised ConvNeXt-Base, supervised SwinV2-Base trained using ImageNet-21k, and CLIP ViT-Base come out on top.
Among smaller backbones evaluated in BoB, ConvNeXt-Tiny and SwinV2-Tiny emerge victorious, followed by DINO ViT-Small.
High-performance convolutional networks pretrained via supervised learning outperform transformers on the majority of tasks considered in BoB.

The observed superiority of supervised pretraining occurs because such models are often trained on larger datasets, and in apples-to-apples comparisons on the same dataset scale, SSL models outperform their supervised counterparts.
ViTs are more sensitive to the amount of pretraining data and the number of parameters than CNNs.
Performance across tasks is strongly correlated, such that the top-performing backbones in BoB tend to be universally good across tasks and settings.

BoB compares many popular publicly available pretrained checkpoints as well as randomly initialized baselines on downstream tasks including image classification on natural, medical, and satellite images, object detection and segmentation, out-of-distribution generalization, and image retrieval.
Three primary factors influence the performance of a pretrained vision backbone: its architecture, the pretraining algorithm, and the pretraining dataset.

claims: BoB benchmarks a diverse suite of pretrained models including vision-language models, self-supervised learning trained models, and the Stable Diffusion backbone across computer vision tasks ranging from classification to object detection to OOD generalization.
BoB's comprehensive analysis was conducted on more than 1500 training runs.

Among the models considered in BoB, convolutional neural networks pretrained in a supervised fashion on large training sets still perform best on most tasks, despite the increasing popularity of vision transformers and self-supervised learning.
In apples-to-apples comparisons on the same architectures and similarly sized pretraining datasets, SSL backbones are highly competitive.

Across the full BoB evaluation suite spanning tasks, datasets, and settings including ID and OOD, supervised ConvNeXt-Base, supervised SwinV2-Base trained using ImageNet-21k, and CLIP ViT-Base come out on top.
Among smaller backbones evaluated in BoB, ConvNeXt-Tiny and SwinV2-Tiny emerge victorious, followed by DINO ViT-Small.
High-performance convolutional networks pretrained via supervised learning outperform transformers on the majority of tasks considered in BoB.

The observed superiority of supervised pretraining occurs because such models are often trained on larger datasets, and in apples-to-apples comparisons on the same dataset scale, SSL models outperform their supervised counterparts.
ViTs are more sensitive to the amount of pretraining data and the number of parameters than CNNs.

claim_records.text: Vision Transformers can be interpreted as ConvNets with dynamic convolutions, enabling characterization of existing Transformers and dynamic ConvNets in a unified framework for side-by-side design choice comparison.
The softmax activation in vision Transformers can be replaced by commonly used ConvNet modules such as ReLU and Layer Normalization, resulting in a faster convergence rate and better performance.
A depth-wise vision Transformer created following the design of depth-wise convolution is more efficient with comparable performance.

The query-key and attention-value matrix multiplications in standard self-attention can be regarded as two 1×1 dynamic convolutions respectively, and the scaled softmax operation can be considered as an activation function, making the self-attention block equivalent to a ConvNet block of static conv → dynamic conv → activation → dynamic conv → static conv.
Replacing softmax with LayerNorm and ReLU in Swin-Tiny, without introducing any computational cost, improves top-1 ImageNet accuracy from 81.13 to 81.56.

The dynamic convolution mechanism in self-attention is unique in that kernels generated from one spatial location are shared with other locations through a global kernel bank, which is more efficient than generating a new set of kernels for each spatial location.

fact_fields.method: unified framework analysis of dynamic convolution mechanisms

claim_records.text: The vanilla ViT has quadratic computational complexity with respect to input resolution, making it prohibitive to serve as a general backbone for computer vision tasks, and usually takes longer to converge during training.

claim_records.text: Analyzing internal representation structure of ViTs and CNNs on image classification benchmarks reveals striking differences between the two architectures, with ViT having more uniform representations across all layers.
Self-attention plays a crucial role in enabling early aggregation of global information in ViTs.
ViT residual connections strongly propagate features from lower to higher layers.
ViTs successfully preserve input spatial information, with noticeable effects from different classification methods.
Using CKA to study internal representation structure, ViTs show a much more uniform similarity structure with a clear grid-like structure compared to ResNets.

fact_fields.method: Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) pairwise layer similarity computation

claim_records.text: Lower and higher layers in ViT show much greater similarity than in ResNet, where similarity is divided into different lower/higher stages.

fact_fields.method: Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) pairwise layer similarity computation

claim_records.text: In cross-model CKA comparisons, the lower half of 60 ResNet layers are similar to approximately the lowest quarter of ViT layers.
Many more lower layers in the ResNet are needed to compute similar representations to the lower layers of ViT.
The top half of the ResNet is approximately similar to the next third of the ViT layers.
Even in the lowest layers of ViT, self-attention layers have a mix of local heads (small distances) and global heads (large distances).

fact_fields.method: attention distance analysis, weighting pixel distances by attention weights for each attention head and averaging over 5000 datapoints

claim_records.text: CNNs are hardcoded to attend only locally in the lower layers, in contrast to ViT lowest layers which have a mix of local and global attention heads.
At higher ViT layers, all self-attention heads are global.
ResNet effective receptive fields are highly local and grow gradually.

claim_records.text: CvT improves Vision Transformer (ViT) in performance and efficiency by introducing convolutions into ViT through two primary modifications: a hierarchy of Transformers containing a new convolutional token embedding, and a convolutional Transformer block leveraging a convolutional projection.

CvT introduces desirable properties of CNNs (shift, scale, and distortion invariance) to the ViT architecture while maintaining the merits of Transformers (dynamic attention, global context, and better generalization).
CvT achieves state-of-the-art performance over other Vision Transformers and ResNets on ImageNet-1k, with fewer parameters and lower FLOPs.
Performance gains of CvT are maintained when pretrained on larger datasets (e.g. ImageNet-22k) and fine-tuned to downstream tasks.
Pre-trained on ImageNet-22k, CvT-W24 obtains a top-1 accuracy of 87.7% on the ImageNet-1k val set.
The positional encoding, a crucial component in existing Vision Transformers, can be safely removed in CvT, simplifying the design for higher resolution vision tasks.
ViT performance is still below similarly sized convolutional neural network (CNN) counterparts (e.g., ResNets) when trained on smaller amounts of data.
CvT does not need position encoding, uses overlapping convolution token embedding, uses convolution projection for attention, and is a hierarchical Transformer.

The Vision Transformer (ViT) decomposes each image into a sequence of tokens (non-overlapping patches) with fixed length, and then applies multiple standard Transformer layers consisting of Multi-Head Self-Attention module (MHSA) and Position-wise Feed-forward module (FFN).
ViT proves that a pure Transformer architecture can attain state-of-the-art performance on image classification when the data is large enough (i.e. on ImageNet-22k, JFT-300M).

BoTNet proposes a backbone architecture that replaces spatial convolutions with global self-attention in the final three bottleneck blocks of a ResNet and achieves strong performance in image recognition.
CvT performs the opposite research direction to works that introduce self-attention to CNNs: it introduces convolutions to Transformers.

claim_records.text: ConTNet achieves 81.8% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, matching DeiT-B, with less than 40% of DeiT-B's computational complexity.
ConTNet-M outperforms ResNet50 as the backbone of Faster-RCNN by 2.6% on the COCO2017 dataset.
ConTNet-M outperforms ResNet50 as the backbone of Mask-RCNN by 3.2% on the COCO2017 dataset.

ConTNet can be optimized like normal ConvNets (e.g., ResNet) and preserves outstanding robustness, unlike transformer-based models such as ViT and DeiT that are sensitive to hyperparameters and heavily dependent on data augmentations when trained from scratch on ImageNet1k.
ConT-M achieves a 1.6% top-1 accuracy improvement over ResNet50 on ImageNet with almost 25% relative savings of computational cost.
ConT-M yields around 3% improvement compared to ResNet-50 based on FCOS and Mask-RCNN for dense prediction tasks.

fact_fields.method: ConT-M as backbone for FCOS and Mask-RCNN

claim_records.text: ConTNet is composed of multiple ConT blocks, each containing two transformer encoder layers and a convolution layer.
In ConTNet, the standard transformer encoder (STE) plays a leading role in capturing contextual features, while conv layers efficiently extract local visual information.
ConTNet gains more performance improvement from strong data augmentation and other training tricks than ResNet, attributed to the overfitting risk of the transformer architecture.
ConTNet is the first exploration to build a neural network with both a standard transformer encoder (STE) and spatial convolution.

claim_records.text: ViT-ResNAS, an efficient multi-stage ViT architecture designed with neural architecture search, achieves better accuracy-MACs and accuracy-throughput trade-offs than original DeiT and other strong ViT baselines on ImageNet.

fact_fields.method: neural architecture search with residual spatial reduction and weight-sharing NAS with multi-architectural sampling

claim_records.text: Residual spatial reduction is proposed to decrease sequence lengths for deeper layers and enable a multi-stage architecture, with skip connections added during length reduction to improve performance and stabilize training of deeper networks.

Weight-sharing NAS with multi-architectural sampling trains a super-network covering all sub-networks by sampling and training multiple sub-networks with one forward-backward pass for efficient super-network training.
Evolutionary search is performed after super-network training to discover high-performance network architectures.
The search space for ViT-ResNAS is constructed by uniformly increasing depth and width of all stages of ViT-Res, with sub-networks defining the search space.

fact_fields.method: search space construction for weight-sharing NAS

claim_records.text: For each stage of ViT-ResNAS, embedding dimension and number of transformer blocks are searched; for different blocks, different numbers of attention heads in MHSA and different hidden sizes in FFN are searched.
The super-network for ViT-ResNAS has the same architecture as the largest network defining the search space, with weights shared across sub-networks.

fact_fields.method: super-network training setup for weight-sharing NAS

claim_records.text: Self-supervised ViT features trained with DINO as k-NN classifiers reach 78.3% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with a small ViT.
DINO-trained ViT-Base achieves 80.1% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet in linear evaluation.
Self-supervised ViT features contain explicit information about the semantic segmentation of an image, which does not emerge as clearly with supervised ViTs nor with convnets.
The DINO neural network g is composed of a backbone f (ViT or ResNet) and a projection head h, with g = h ◦ f, and downstream task features are the backbone f output.
The DINO projection head consists of a 3-layer MLP with hidden dimension 2048 followed by l2 normalization and a weight normalized fully connected layer with K dimensions.
DINO does not use a predictor, resulting in the exact same architecture in both student and teacher networks.
When applying DINO to ViT, no batch normalization is used in projection heads, making the system entirely BN-free.
The ViT architecture takes as input a grid of non-overlapping contiguous image patches, typically using patch resolution N=16 ("/16") or N=8 ("/8") in this work.
An extra learnable token ([CLS]) is added to the ViT patch embedding sequence to aggregate information from the entire sequence, and the projection head h is attached at its output.
ViTs have not yet delivered clear benefits over convnets: they are computationally more demanding, require more training data, and their features do not exhibit unique properties.
Image-level supervision often reduces the rich visual information contained in an image to a single concept selected from a predefined set of a few thousand object categories.

claim_records.text: MobileViT achieves top-1 accuracy of 78.4% on ImageNet-1k with about 6 million parameters.
MobileViT is 3.2% more accurate than MobileNetv3 and 6.2% more accurate than DeIT on ImageNet-1k for a similar number of parameters.
MobileViT is 5.7% more accurate than MobileNetv3 on the MS-COCO object detection task for a similar number of parameters.
Replacing MNASNet with MobileViT as a feature backbone in SSDLite results in a detection network that is +1.8% mAP better and 1.8× smaller.
For a parameter budget of about 5-6 million, MobileViT achieves 78.4% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1k, with a simpler training recipe than MobileNetv3 (300 vs 600 epochs; 1024 vs 4096 batch size).
The computational cost of self-attention in standard vision transformers is O(N²d), where N is the number of patches and d is the fixed projection dimension.
DPT, a ViT-based network, learns 6× more parameters than DeepLabv3 (345 M vs 59 M) to deliver similar segmentation performance.

ViT models are sensitive to L2 regularization and require extensive data augmentation to prevent overfitting, while MobileViT models train with basic augmentation and are less sensitive to L2 regularization.

MobileViT block replaces local processing in convolutions with global processing using transformers, combining CNN- and ViT-like properties to learn better representations with fewer parameters and simple training recipes.

claim_records.text: The transformer architecture has been used as a replacement for widely used convolution operators due to its ability to learn long-range dependencies.
The replacement of convolution operators by transformers was proven successful in numerous tasks, with several state-of-the-art methods relying on transformers for better learning.
The 3D computer vision field has witnessed an increase in employing transformers for 3D convolution neural networks and multi-layer perceptron networks.
3D vision requires special attention compared to general vision transformers due to differences in data representation and processing relative to 2D vision.
The presented systematic review covers more than 100 transformer methods for different 3D vision tasks including classification, segmentation, detection, completion, and pose estimation.
Transformer design in 3D vision allows processing of data with various 3D representations.
The survey compares performance of transformer-based 3D vision methods to common non-transformer methods on 12 3D benchmarks to assess competitiveness.

claim_records.text: The survey concludes by discussing different open directions and challenges for transformers in 3D vision.

claims: A pure Transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches performs very well on image classification tasks, removing the prior reliance on CNNs for vision Transformer applications.

When pre-trained on large amounts of data and transferred to mid-sized or small image recognition benchmarks, Vision Transformer (ViT) attains excellent results compared to state-of-the-art convolutional networks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources to train.

Prior vision works either applied attention in conjunction with convolutional networks, or used attention to replace certain convolutional components while retaining the overall convolutional network structure.
Vision Transformers dominate ResNets on the performance/compute trade-off, using approximately 2-4× less compute to attain the same performance averaged over 5 datasets.
Hybrid ResNet-ViT models slightly outperform pure ViT at small computational budgets, but this performance difference vanishes for larger models.
Vision Transformers do not show performance saturation within the tested pre-training compute range, motivating future scaling efforts.

The Vision Transformer reshapes input images into flattened 2D patch sequences, maps patches to a constant latent dimension D via trainable linear projection, and prepends a learnable class token whose final encoder state serves as the image representation.

Vision Transformer introduces no image-specific inductive biases into the architecture apart from the initial patch extraction step, processing images as patch sequences via a standard Transformer encoder as used in NLP.
Vision Transformer matches or exceeds the state of the art on many image classification datasets while being relatively cheap to pre-train.

Prior hybrid CNN-Transformer vision models that replaced convolutions entirely have not been scaled effectively on modern hardware accelerators due to use of specialized attention patterns, leaving classic ResNet-like architectures as state of the art for large-scale image recognition prior to this work.
Convolutional architectures remained dominant in computer vision at the time of the study, even as Transformer models scaled to 100B parameters in NLP with no sign of saturating performance.

claim_records.text: The routine of the current ViT model is to maintain a full-length patch sequence during inference, which is redundant and lacks hierarchical representation.

The proposed Hierarchical Visual Transformer (HVT) progressively pools visual tokens to shrink the sequence length and hence reduces the computational cost, analogous to the feature maps downsampling in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs).

HVT brings the benefit that model capacity can be increased by scaling dimensions of depth/width/resolution/patch size without introducing extra computational complexity due to the reduced sequence length.
The average pooled visual tokens contain more discriminative information than the single class token.
With comparable FLOPs, HVT outperforms the competitive baselines on ImageNet and CIFAR-100 datasets for the image classification task.

claim_records.text: Vision Transformers' inherent reliance on sequential input enforces the manual partitioning of images into patch sequences, which disrupts the image's inherent structural and semantic continuity.
The proposed Pattern Transformer (Patternformer) adaptively converts images to pattern sequences for Transformer input.

Patternformer employs a Convolutional Neural Network to extract various patterns from the input image, with each channel representing a unique pattern that is fed into the succeeding Transformer as a visual token.
By enabling the network to optimize these patterns, each pattern concentrates on its local region of interest, thereby preserving its intrinsic structural and semantic information.
Only employing the vanilla ResNet and Transformer, Patternformer has accomplished state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

claim_records.text: Swin Transformer achieves 87.3 top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K image classification.
Swin Transformer achieves 58.7 box AP on COCO test-dev for object detection.
Swin Transformer achieves 51.1 mask AP on COCO test-dev for object detection.
Swin Transformer achieves 53.5 mIoU on ADE20K val for semantic segmentation.
The shifted windowing scheme in Swin Transformer brings greater efficiency by limiting self-attention computation to non-overlapping local windows while also allowing for cross-window connection.
The hierarchical Swin Transformer architecture has linear computational complexity with respect to image size.
Existing Transformer-based models use tokens of fixed scale, a property unsuitable for vision applications where visual elements vary substantially in scale.
The computational complexity of standard Transformer self-attention is quadratic to image size, making dense prediction on high-resolution images intractable.

Swin Transformer builds hierarchical feature maps by merging image patches in deeper layers and has linear computation complexity to input image size due to self-attention computation only within each local window.
Previous vision Transformers produce feature maps of a single low resolution and have quadratic computation complexity to input image size due to global self-attention computation.

A Swin Transformer block consists of a shifted window based MSA module, followed by a 2-layer MLP with GELU non-linearity, with LayerNorm applied before each module and residual connections after each module.

Swin Transformer has the same feature map resolutions as typical convolutional networks such as VGG and ResNet, allowing it to conveniently replace existing backbone networks for various vision tasks.
Prior works that compute self-attention within a local window of each pixel achieve slightly better accuracy/FLOPs trade-offs than the counterpart ResNet architecture.

claim_records.text: Visual Prompt Tuning (VPT) introduces only a small amount (less than 1% of model parameters) of trainable parameters in the input space while keeping the model backbone frozen, as an efficient and effective alternative to full fine-tuning for large-scale Transformer models in vision.
VPT achieves significant performance gains compared to other parameter efficient tuning protocols across extensive experiments on a wide variety of downstream recognition tasks.
VPT outperforms full fine-tuning in many cases across model capacities and training data scales, while reducing per-task storage cost.
ViT-Huge has 632M parameters, which is significantly larger than the 25M parameters of ResNet-50.
VPT-deep enables linearly separable representations while using less parameters than full fine-tuning.
Adding extra tunable parameters for every Transformer layer (VPT-deep) improves performance compared to VPT-shallow, which only inserts prompts for the first layer's input.
On Clevr/count, VPT-deep and full fine-tuning recover the underlying manifold structure of the task, unlike VPT-shallow and Linear.
The ADE20K semantic segmentation task is evaluated with the SETR-PUP Transformer model, which adds a standard ConvNet head to the ViT backbone to perform segmentation.
Full fine-tuning of the pre-trained model requires storing and deploying a separate copy of the backbone parameters for every single task.
All backbones used in the experiment are pre-trained on ImageNet-21k, including Vision Transformers (ViT) and Swin Transformers (Swin).
The Full fine-tuning protocol fully updates all backbone and classification head parameters.
The Linear baseline treats the pre-trained backbone as a feature extractor with fixed weights during tuning, using only a linear layer as the classification head.
VPT works well in the larger ConvNet backbone ConvNeXt-B (pre-trained on ImageNet-21k), offering accuracy gains over other sparse tuning protocols and outperforming Full on 8 out of 19 cases.
The advantages of VPT diminish with the smaller ConvNet ResNet-50 (pre-trained on ImageNet-1k), as there is no clear winner for all 19 VTAB-1k tasks.
The value of p (number of learnable prompt pixels) in the VPT experiment is 2 orders of magnitude smaller than previous work, e.g., 5 vs. 263.

ViT-Huge has 632M parameters, which is significantly larger than the 25M parameters of ResNet-50.
VPT-deep enables linearly separable representations while using less parameters than full fine-tuning.
Adding extra tunable parameters for every Transformer layer (VPT-deep) improves performance compared to VPT-shallow, which only inserts prompts for the first layer's input.
On Clevr/count, VPT-deep and full fine-tuning recover the underlying manifold structure of the task, unlike VPT-shallow and Linear.
The ADE20K semantic segmentation task is evaluated with the SETR-PUP Transformer model, which adds a standard ConvNet head to the ViT backbone to perform segmentation.
Full fine-tuning of the pre-trained model requires storing and deploying a separate copy of the backbone parameters for every single task.
All backbones used in the experiment are pre-trained on ImageNet-21k, including Vision Transformers (ViT) and Swin Transformers (Swin).
The Full fine-tuning protocol fully updates all backbone and classification head parameters.
The Linear baseline treats the pre-trained backbone as a feature extractor with fixed weights during tuning, using only a linear layer as the classification head.
VPT works well in the larger ConvNet backbone ConvNeXt-B (pre-trained on ImageNet-21k), offering accuracy gains over other sparse tuning protocols and outperforming Full on 8 out of 19 cases.
The advantages of VPT diminish with the smaller ConvNet ResNet-50 (pre-trained on ImageNet-1k), as there is no clear winner for all 19 VTAB-1k tasks.
The value of p (number of learnable prompt pixels) in the VPT experiment is 2 orders of magnitude smaller than previous work, e.g., 5 vs. 263.

claim_records.text: Depthwise separable convolutions (DSC) make CNNs more efficient in time and memory complexity without deteriorating their accuracy, and sometimes even improving it, as an approximation of regular convolution.
Implementing DSC into the Pretrained Audio Neural Networks (PANN) family for audio classification on AudioSet shows benefits in terms of accuracy/model size trade-off.
The adapted ConvNeXt model rapidly overfits on the audio classification task on AudioSet.
The best ConvNeXt model reached 0.471 mean-average precision on AudioSet, which is better than or equivalent to recent large audio transformers, while using three times less parameters.
The adapted ConvNeXt model achieved positive results in audio captioning and audio retrieval tasks.

claim_records.text: The exploration from a standard ResNet toward vision Transformer design produces a family of pure ConvNet models named ConvNeXt.

fact_fields.method: Gradual modernization of a standard ResNet toward vision Transformer design

claim_records.text: Hierarchical Transformers such as Swin Transformers reintroduced several ConvNet priors, making Transformers practically viable as a generic vision backbone.
Vision Transformers quickly superseded ConvNets as the state-of-the-art image classification model after the start of the Roaring 20s of visual recognition.
ViT introduces no image-specific inductive bias and makes minimal changes to the original NLP Transformers, except for the initial patchify layer that splits an image into a sequence of patches.
With larger model and dataset sizes, Transformers can outperform standard ResNets by a significant margin on image classification tasks.
ViT's global attention design has quadratic complexity with respect to input size, which is acceptable for ImageNet classification but quickly becomes intractable with higher-resolution inputs.

The exploration considers two model sizes in terms of FLOPs: one around 4.5×10^9 FLOPs corresponding to ResNet-50 / Swin-T regime, and another around 15.0×10^9 FLOPs corresponding to ResNet-200 / Swin-B regime.

fact_fields.method: Roadmap exploration from ResNet to a ConvNet resembling Transformers

claim_records.text: ConvNeXt achieves ImageNet-1K classification accuracy significantly exceeding Swin-T's 81.3% in the ResNet-50 / Swin-T compute regime.

ConvNeXt has approximately the same FLOPs, parameter count, throughput, and memory use as the Swin Transformer, but does not require specialized modules such as shifted window attention or relative position biases.

For ResNet-200 regime experiments, changing the stage block ratio from (3, 24, 36, 3) to Swin-B's (3, 3, 27, 3) drastically reduces FLOPs, so width is increased from 64 to 84 to keep FLOPs at a similar level.
Inverting dimensions brings a larger improvement at the ResNet-200 regime than at the ResNet-50 regime, with +0.79% versus +0.14%.

fact_fields.method: Dimension inversion step in modernization roadmap

claim_records.text: After adopting depthwise convolutions in the ResNet-200 regime, width is further increased to 128, matching Swin-B's width.

claim_records.text: Low-resolution pretrained ConvNeXt underperforms when directly applied on high resolution, so ConvLLaVA updates it to bridge the gap.

claim_records.text: ConvLLaVA supports inputs of 1536x1536 resolution generating only 576 visual tokens, capable of handling images of arbitrary aspect ratios.

claim_records.text: The reference convolution-free DeiT vision transformer with 86M parameters achieves 83.1% top-1 accuracy under single-crop evaluation on ImageNet, with no external training data.
DeiT models can be trained on a single computer in less than 3 days.
When using the proposed token-based distillation strategy, DeiT achieves up to 85.2% accuracy on ImageNet.
The DeiT-S and DeiT-Ti models are trained on a single node with 4 GPUs in three days, with parameter counts comparable to ResNet-50 and ResNet-18 respectively.
The proposed transformer-specific distillation strategy outperforms vanilla distillation by a significant margin.
With the proposed distillation approach, image transformers learn more from a convnet teacher than from another transformer with comparable performance.
DeiT achieves a 6.3% top-1 accuracy improvement over previous ViT models trained on ImageNet-1k only in a comparable setting.
DeiT⚗, produced via distillation from a relatively weaker RegNetY, outperforms the EfficientNet convnet on ImageNet.

fact_fields.method: Distillation from RegNetY teacher to DeiT student (DeiT⚗)

claim_records.text: DeiT⚗ outperforms the ViT-B model pre-trained on JFT300M at resolution 384 by 1% top-1 accuracy (85.2% vs 84.15%), while being significantly faster to train.

HTR-ConvText introduces the ConvText encoder, a hybrid architecture combining global context and local features within a hierarchical structure that reduces sequence length for improved efficiency.

claim_records.text: Most off-the-shelf Vision Transformers, particularly CLIP, run at 224 times 224px resolution.
High-resolution versions of off-the-shelf Vision Transformers are around 378-448px but remain inflexible.
The introduced method coherently and cheaply upsamples feature maps of low-resolution vision encoders while picking up fine-grained details that would otherwise be lost due to resolution.
The upsampling method is demonstrated on core perception tasks and within agglomerative model training using RADIO to provide richer targets for distillation.
Vision Transformers trained using contrastive loss such as CLIP are the frontier of general purpose vision backbones in computer vision.

claim_records.text: ViT achieves inferior performance to CNNs when trained from scratch on a midsize dataset like ImageNet.
The simple tokenization of input images in ViT fails to model important local structure such as edges and lines among neighboring pixels, leading to low training sample efficiency.
The redundant attention backbone design of ViT leads to limited feature richness for fixed computation budgets and limited training samples.

T2T-ViT incorporates a layer-wise Tokens-to-Token (T2T) transformation that progressively structurizes the image to tokens by recursively aggregating neighboring Tokens into one Token, such that local structure represented by surrounding tokens can be modeled and tokens length can be reduced.
T2T-ViT reduces the parameter count and MACs of vanilla ViT by half, while achieving more than 3.0% improvement when trained from scratch on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT outperforms ResNets and achieves comparable performance with MobileNets by directly training on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT with comparable size to ResNet50 (21.5M parameters) achieves 83.3% top1 accuracy at image resolution 384×384 on ImageNet.
T2T-ViT-14, T2T-ViT-19 and T2T-ViT-24 are designed to have comparable parameters with ResNet50, ResNet101 and ResNet152 respectively.

T2T-ViT-7 and T2T-ViT-12 are lite models with comparable model size to MobileNetV1 and MobileNetV2, with no special efficient convolution designs and only reduced layer depth, hidden dimension, and MLP ratio.

Five architecture designs borrowed from CNNs were explored for ViT backbone: Dense connection as DenseNet, deep-narrow vs. shallow-wide structure as in Wide-ResNets, channel attention as Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks, more split heads in multi-head attention layer as ResNeXt, and Ghost operations as GhostNet.

claim_records.text: Among the explored CNN-inspired designs, the deep-narrow structure is the most efficient and effective for ViT, reducing parameter count and MACs significantly with nearly no degradation in performance.

DPN-131 further pushes the state-of-the-art single model performance on ImageNet-1k with about 2 times faster training speed.
DPN demonstrates consistently better performance than DenseNet, ResNet and ResNeXt on Places365 scene classification, PASCAL VOC detection, and PASCAL VOC segmentation tasks.
